tags.description: Classic Mediterranean wall dive on a rocky bar resembling a ship's hull (hence the name), 10-38m. Posidonia seagrass meadows on shallow plateau, coralligenous cliff face 15-20m tall on the east side down to a sand bottom at 38m. Groupers, morays, and amberjacks in wall crevices. Excellent macro photography and light penetration. 15m+ visibility typical.

tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-08-25. RESOLVED a prior flagged conflict: previous QA compared dive-operator facts against the generic English Wikipedia ship article and found a date/route mismatch. Live re-check found the correct, dedicated French Wikipedia wreck article (fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagona_(épave)), which fully corroborates the dive-operator sources: built 1912, Dundee Shipbuilding Co., 53.30m x 8.60m, 808 tons, sank 3 Dec 1945 near Port-Cros/Porquerolles by mine, 2 dead + 1 missing, wreck depth 35-47m. CORRECTED ship-type/history: the wiki article documents the Sagona as a bulk cargo steamer (not a passenger/freight ferry as previously described) that changed hands between Newfoundland Produce Co., Reid Newfoundland Co. (1914), the Newfoundland government (1923), Colliford Clarke Co. of London (1941), and finally the Greek-operated Zarati/Zaratti Steamship Co.; it served seal-hunting and rescue operations under Newfoundland ownership. Dimensions refined to 53.30m x 8.60m (from rounded 54m x 8.5m).

Re-audited 2026-08-25. Site is generally listed by operators as "Pointe de la Croix" (added as alt_name) rather than "Ilot de la Croix" -- same location, confirmed by cross-referencing coordinates and description against aquabormes.fr, destination.portcros-parcnational.fr, miopalmoplongee.com and hyeres-plongee.com. White gorgonians (Eunicella singularis) re-confirmed as the defining feature, explicitly contrasted with the red gorgonians at La Gabiniere. Depth 30m and site area ~12,000 sq m confirmed by destination.portcros-parcnational.fr. Current typically flows east to west toward Porquerolles.

Re-audited 2026-08-25. Official park page (portcros-parcnational.fr) confirms the marked underwater trail itself is a free, unguided snorkeling route (mask/fins/snorkel), open 15 June-15 September, ~40 minutes, 6 submerged buoys with info panels, average trail depth not exceeding ~4m. Species per habitat zone confirmed site-specific: posidonia beds hide sea urchins and fan mussels plus castagnoles/green wrasse/sars/saupes; dark crevices hold encrusting anemones and sponges; shallow lit rock has wrasse, scorpionfish, starfish; deeper scree (beyond the marked trail, within the wider bay/dive site) has groupers, moray eels, and octopus. The '180 fish species' figure is a Port-Cros park-wide total (not a La Palud-specific species list) -- description reworded to attribute it correctly.
tags.description: Shore-accessible site in protected marine reserve with a free marked snorkeling trail (6 buoys, ~40 min, avg depth ~4m, open 15 Jun-15 Sep), plus deeper scuba exploration to 12m. Beginner-friendly posidonia seagrass exploration with castagnoles, green wrasse, sars and saupes; groupers, moray eels and octopus in the deeper scree beyond the marked trail.

tags.name: Wildcat
tags.qa_note: Re-audited 2026-08-25 -- IMPORTANT REVERSAL of a prior conclusion. The previous QA pass stated the '15 August 1944 crash' theory was 'incorrectly attributed' and had no source. Live re-search found a genuine, independent source for it: cirkwi.com, citing US archives, gives a specific, detailed account -- Wildcat V, 882 Naval Air Squadron, HMS Searcher (escort carrier), crashed 15 Aug 1944 on a reconnaissance mission during Operation Dragoon, pilot recovered. This is NOT the same as the earlier mis-citation (which wrongly pinned the claim on bormesplongee.fr) -- it is a real, separately sourced competing theory that must be presented, not dismissed. Meanwhile destination.portcros-parcnational.fr (official park site), aquabormes.fr and tribloo.com all independently describe a 1950s jettison-from-carrier theory (aircraft possibly served post-war aboard the French carrier Hermes before being scrapped at sea, no confirmed date). Both theories are now documented in the markdown as an unresolved conflict per anti-hallucination policy -- neither is presented as fact. Armament CORRECTED: official park source and tribloo.com both independently give 4 x 12.7mm machine guns plus 2 x 45kg bombs; the prior '6 machine guns total' figure came from an unsourced AI search synthesis, not a fetched primary source, and has been dropped. Dimensions refined: wingspan ~11.6m (sources round to 'over 11m' or '12m'), length ~8.8m (sources round to 'over 8m' or '9m') -- matches real F4F/Martlet V specs. Depth reported inconsistently across sources (51m, 52m, 53m, 54m) -- using 51-54m range; depth field set to 54m (destination.portcros-parcnational.fr, official park source) as primary. Marine life also revised: sources disagree, from tribloo.com's 'nothing exceptional, a few conger eels and mullet' to aquabormes.fr's fuller list including lobster/galatheas -- description now presents this as a range rather than a single confident list, and 'groupers' has been dropped as it appeared in only one lower-confidence generic synthesis, not a directly fetched primary source.
